subject: humanities
passage: Around 1562 the young Mughal emperor Akbar commissioned an illustrated copy of the Hamzanama, a sprawling adventure romance, and the project occupied his imperial workshop for roughly fifteen years. Supervised first by Mir Sayyid Ali and later by Abd al-Samad, two Persian masters whom Akbar's father, Humayun, had brought to India, more than one hundred artists, most of them trained in Indian painting traditions, produced some 1,400 large paintings on cotton cloth for the project. Only about 200 of ______ survive today, scattered among museums and private collections around the world.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: What survives today is a number of the paintings: "Only about 200 of ______" refers back to "some 1,400 large paintings." That antecedent is plural, and the pronoun is the object of the preposition "of," so it must be the plural object pronoun "them." The singular nouns "project," "workshop" and "Hamzanama" are tempting, but you can't have "200 of" a single project.
explanation.A: Correct. The plural object pronoun "them" refers to the plural "paintings" and correctly follows the preposition "of."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Its" is a singular possessive that must be followed by a noun, so "200 of its" is incomplete and doesn't match the plural "paintings."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "They" is a subject pronoun, so it can't be the object of the preposition "of"; "200 of they" is not standard.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "It" is singular and would point to the project or the Hamzanama, but the 200 surviving items are some of the plural "paintings."
